content: All, everything that I understand, I understand only because I love.
author: Leo Tolstoy
story:
Despite global literary fame and vast aristocratic estates at Yasnaya Polyana, Tolstoy suffered a devastating midlife existential crisis in the 1870s that brought him to the brink of suicide. Renouncing his wealth and copyrights, he adopted peasant garb to live out the radical Sermon on the Mount, pioneering the philosophy of nonviolent resistance that later inspired Gandhi.

Exploring the mysteries of human connection, Leo Tolstoy saw that genuine fulfillment cannot be hoarded or manufactured through egoic control. It blossoms only when we lower our defenses, dissolve self-importance, and meet the world with openhearted generosity.
reflectionPrompt: What defensive wall or grudge are you holding onto that is keeping genuine warmth and intimacy away?
